died.name: Thomas Washington Barber
died.cause: shot along with his horse by slavery supporters near Lawrence, Kansas

died.name: Jefferson Davis
died.desc: President of the Confederate States of America

died.name: Vince Coleman
died.cause: warning an incoming train by telegraph of the impending Halifax Explosion
died.last_words: Hold up the train. Ammunition ship afire in harbour making for Pier 6 and will explode. Guess this will be my last message. Goodbye, boys.

died.name: Lead Belly
died.desc: American folk and blues singer, musician and songwriter
died.last_words: Doctor, if I put this here guitar down now, I ain't never gonna wake up.

died.name: Marc Lépine
died.desc: Canadian perpetrator of the École Polytechnique massacre
died.cause: in which he killed fourteen women, before fatally shooting himself

born.name: Guillaume-Chrétien de Lamoignon de Malesherbes
born.desc: French statesman and government minister, defense counsel of Louis XVI
born.cause: to the priest prior to his execution by guillotine
born.last_words: Hold your tongue! your wretched chatter disgusts me.

born.name: William Ledyard
born.desc: American soldier, lieutenant colonel in the Connecticut militia
born.cause: surrendering Fort Griswold during the Battle of Groton Heights. The British officer to whom Ledyard gave his sword in surrender immediately killed him with it
born.last_words: I did, sir, but you do now.

born.name: Luigi Lablache
born.cause: After singing the first stanza of Home! Sweet Home! on his deathbed, his voice failed at the start of the second stanza
born.last_words: Mid pleasures and palaces though we may roam / Be it ever so humble, there's no place like home / A charm from the skies seems to hallow us there / Which seek thro' the world, is ne'er met elsewhere / Home! Home! / Sweet, sweet home! / There's no place like home / There's no place like home!
